conviction_note: Nineteen analysts cover this bank and their Modular Finance consensus (published 19 Oct) is the bar. The only lean comes from the company's own 30 Sep pre-close call: it guided to NII headwinds 'similar to Q2'. In Q2 a similar pre-close was followed by flat NII despite comparable FX and day-count tailwinds, so a +170m QoQ NII consensus looks about 150m rich. Habitual beats on costs and credit losses mostly offset that, so print_vs_bar is about -0.3% on operating profit. abs_move_pct is set from the name's own report-day moves (median 2.95%, mean 4.1%, tail -9.1/+7.0/+8.0), raised for new numbers. p_up is 47 because the lean is an inference, and Citi sits 1-2% above consensus on NII, which is a credible counter-view.

already_public.what: Pre-close call: Q3 NII headwinds from higher funding costs and corporate repricing lag 'similar to Q2'; +1 day (SEK 20-30m/day); weaker SEK a tailwind; corporate volumes down since Q2; savings fees expected up; NFT averages SEK 500-600m/quarter; CET1 Q2 17.2%, 250bp over SREP; new Pillar 2 corporate models net neutral in Q3 (AI-generated Quartr summary, not the transcript)
Q2 2026 interim report: operating profit 6,678m, H1 anticipated dividend SEK 4.77 (82% payout), CET1 2.50pp above requirement, within 1-3pp target range
Report date and time confirmed: 07:00 CET Wednesday 21 October, presentation 08:15

new_in_release.expect: NII about flat QoQ near 10.0bn against a 10,178m consensus, so a small miss. Costs and credit losses come in below consensus (5,878m / 107m) as in Q1 and Q2. NFT is uncertain against 516m. Operating profit lands within about 1% of 7,369m.
Q3 dividend accrual under the high-payout policy. The direction of any extra-distribution signal is unknown. A 120m-share buyback mandate exists from the 2026 AGM, but I found no launched programme.
None. Handelsbanken gives no numerical guide, so expect commentary on NII sensitivity to the expected Riksbank hikes.

Capital: REA down about SEK 1.3bn from sovereign exposures moving to standardised models, which the company has already disclosed. Read-across from Nordea's ECB-driven buyback halt does not apply directly, because Handelsbanken is supervised by Finansinspektionen.

findings.finding: Management's own pre-close call guided Q3 NII headwinds 'similar to Q2' (funding costs, corporate repricing lag, falling corporate volumes). Q2 delivered flat NII (10,016m to 10,008m) despite a weaker SEK (Q2/Q1 average EURSEK +1.9%, NOKSEK +5.7%, GBPSEK +2.1%) and an extra day. Q3 has similar tailwinds (EURSEK +2.0%, NOKSEK +2.3%, GBPSEK +3.2%), which again points to about 10.0bn against a consensus of 10,178m (+1.7% QoQ).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: NII -1.5% vs consensus (10,008 vs 10,164) plus an NFT miss, and the stock fell 3.5% on the day. Q1 2026: NII +0.7% vs consensus, stock -0.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus (published 19 Oct, after the pre-close) still models +170m QoQ NII. If the pre-close had been taken at face value, the NII line would sit near 10.0bn. The stock is also near its 60-day high (+7.1% over 60 days), not discounting a second consecutive NII miss.
findings.independence: Placera/Finwire Q1 and Q2 results tables give the NII series and the prior consensus misses: https://www.placera.se/nyheter/handelsbanken-minskar-rorelseresultatet-2026-07-15 . The FX series is Yahoo EURSEK=X / NOKSEK=X / GBPSEK=X daily closes. A counter-view comes from a different source: Citi (8 Oct) is 1-2% ABOVE consensus on NII and fees: https://www.placera.se/telegram/handelsbanken-citi-hojer-riktkursen-for-handelsbanken-till-127-kronor-fran-118-kronor-upprepar-salj-20261008

findings.finding: Handelsbanken has beaten Modular consensus on costs and on credit losses in both 2026 quarters (costs 5,838 vs 5,990 and 5,963 vs 6,063; credit losses 35 vs 121 and 30 vs 122). Q3 consensus again carries credit losses of 107m, and costs of 5,878m against a seasonally lower Q3 (Q3-25 5,855m). Repeating that pattern adds about SEK 100-170m, roughly 1.5-2% of operating profit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 operating profit beat by 3.4%, driven by costs and credit losses, yet the stock fell 0.5%. Low-quality beats have not been paid here.
findings.original_quote: Rörelsekostnaderna uppgick till -5 838 miljoner kronor (-6 162), analytikerkonsensus var -5 990 miljoner kronor. Kreditförlusterna uppgick till -35 miljoner kronor. ... Väntat var kreditförluster på -121 miljoner kronor. (Operating costs were SEK -5,838m (-6,162), analyst consensus was -5,990m. Credit losses were -35m ... credit losses of -121m had been expected.)
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus credit losses of 107m are close to the 121-122m that was wrong twice this year, so analysts have not moved the line. If the pattern were priced, the Modular credit-loss line would be near 30-40m.
findings.independence: Q2 table from a separate article: https://www.placera.se/nyheter/handelsbanken-minskar-rorelseresultatet-2026-07-15 (same publisher, different quarter).

findings.finding: Nordea's Q3 release (15 Oct) reported its net fair value result down 19% y/y 'due to extraordinary interest rate volatility'. That is a read-across risk to Handelsbanken's NFT consensus of 516m, a line Handelsbanken missed by 79% in Q2 (116 vs 551).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: NFT 116m vs 551m consensus, the largest single miss in a print that fell 3.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus NFT (516m) sits inside management's 500-600m 'normal' band and assumes no Q3 volatility hit. A priced view would show a lower NFT line in the 19 Oct consensus.
findings.independence: none (a proxy from one counterparty; Handelsbanken's NFT is driven by hedge accounting and treasury rather than market-making)

findings.finding: The Stockholm index averaged 3,251.6 in Q3 against 3,108.7 in Q2 (+4.6%), and Nordea reported savings income +14% y/y. That supports AUM-linked fees against a consensus of 3,214m (+2.5% QoQ). Handelsbanken has beaten fee consensus in Q1 (+1.5%) and Q2 (+0.9%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fee beats of 0.9-1.5% in 2026 did not decide either report day.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: consensus already models a fee rise and Citi is only 1-2% above it. Filed because it is the one line where both the index and the peer point the same way.
findings.independence: Nordea Q3 savings income +14%: https://www.nordea.com/en/press/2026-10-15/third-quarter-results-2026 ; management guided savings fees up on the pre-close: https://quartr.com/events/handelsbanken-shb-pre-close-call_3gymvdY4

findings.finding: Nordea halted buybacks on 15 Oct pending an ECB review of its capital base and fell about 7-8% that day, which shows the Nordic bank tape trading the capital-return line. Handelsbanken is supervised by Finansinspektionen, not the ECB, and reported CET1 2.5pp above requirement with an 82% H1 payout accrual, so the read-across has no sign.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Capital-return news drove the largest report-day moves in the Modular history: Q2-2025 -9.1%, Q1-2025 +7.0%, Q3-2024 +8.0%. These are inferred from size, and the drivers were not individually verified.
findings.original_quote: Allerdings sollen vorerst keine weiteren eigenen Aktien zurückgekauft werden ... wegen der derzeit laufenden Überprüfung der Kapitalbasis durch die Europäische Zentralbank (EZB). (However, no further own shares are to be bought back for now ... because of the ECB's ongoing review of the capital base.)
findings.why_not_priced: SHB fell 1.7% on 15 Oct and recovered 1.7% on 16 Oct, so the market has already decided the halt is Nordea-specific. Sized at 0 for that reason; filed because the line is where the tail sits and it feeds abs_move_pct.

baseline_tension: The lean is flat (priced_lean +0.03, run-up -0.6% over 20 days, +7.1% over 60 days) and the register gives no anchor. The slight negative NII lean agrees with the bearish sell-side (every target below spot) rather than cutting against it, which is a reason to keep p_up near 50.
language_note: The Swedish Finwire/Modular consensus table (Borsvarlden, 19 Oct) carried the line-by-line bar (NII 10,178, fees 3,214, NFT 516, costs 5,878, credit losses 107, operating profit 7,369) and eight quarters of actual report-day moves. No English source surfaced either.
Swedish Placera/Finwire results tables for Q1 and Q2 2026 gave the consensus misses and beats by line, which is the basis of the cost and credit-loss pattern finding.

The Swedish Finwire note on Citi (8 Oct) carried 'Citi ligger 1–2 procent över konsensus för räntenetto och provisionsintäkter' (Citi is 1-2% above consensus on NII and fees), the main counter to the NII finding.
Filings themselves (Nasdaq Nordic, Cision) were bilingual, with nothing in the Swedish version that the English one lacked.
lessons_applied: 'Too small about the move; size on what is new, let history move p_up': abs_move_pct raised from 3.5 to 4.0, set from the name's actual report-day moves (median 2.95, mean 4.1, tail 9.1) rather than the baseline's 1.58 cadence estimate.
'A beat made of a one-off is sold': the cost/credit-loss finding was cut from +0.3 to +0.2, because a credit-loss beat is low quality and Q1's 3.4% beat was met with -0.5%.
'A narrow proxy loses / macro transmission is a hypothesis': the Nordea NFT read-across went from -0.2 to -0.1 and the index-to-fees finding from +0.2 to +0.1.
p_up left at 47: the reaction history is mixed and the lean is inference, not a company number.
